version.changelog:
sleep-story-voice v0.1.1

- Adds detailed instructions for generating spoken clips from pre-written short sleep stories.
- Clarifies scope to cover only short stories with proper routing for other narration types.
- Enforces required inputs: written stories, pronunciation tables for names, clip count, and voice rights.
- Documents step-by-step flow for free listen list planning, voice cloning consent, credit checking, and delivery.
- Mandates using package-bundled MCP client for all remote Beatra operations (no REST/OpenAPI fallback).
- Expands documentation on automatic updates, error recovery, and billing workflow.

llm.summary: The skill is mostly disclosed and not clearly malicious, but it asks for broad shared Beatra authority and silently updates its own package despite being advertised as a narrow sleep-story voice tool.

dimensions.detail: The client records and transmits package, platform, and installation registration metadata; this is documented and limited, but it is extra telemetry for a content-generation skill.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The package uses standard-library scripts rather than hidden installers, but authorization creates shared state under ~/.beatra and normal client use performs silent update checks and automatic package replacement by default.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The workflow includes good user-approval controls for paid clone and speech calls, but the bundled client exposes a generic Beatra MCP call surface beyond the named sleep-story operations.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill persists a full-scope shared bearer token, local inventory and registration state, update state, and has uninstall logic that can revoke and remove shared connection files when it decides this is the last Beatra skill.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is generating spoken sleep-story clips, but the authorization scope includes image, video, music, artifact, wallet, task-cancel, speech, and voice permissions through one shared device token.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review this before installing as a shared, full-scope Beatra client rather than just a sleep-story voice helper. Install only if you are comfortable with a persistent ~/.beatra device token, broad media-generation and wallet/task permissions, Beatra registration metadata, local sample uploads when cloning is requested, and silent package self-updates unless you turn them off with the documented command.
llm.findings:
[LP3] unexpected: Verified that network, shell execution, local state writes, and credential-backed MCP calls are required; some are expected for a hosted voice service, but the total authority is broader than a narrow voice-pack skill needs.
[TP4] unexpected: Verified authentication, persistent shared credentials, upload, registration, general MCP calls, and self-update behavior. These are disclosed, so this is not treated as deception, but the scope materially exceeds the short description.
[SDI-1] unexpected: authorize.py requests a single broad scope set including non-speech media generation, artifact access, wallet spending, and task cancellation; several of these are not required by the sleep-story workflow.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Image, video, and music generation scopes are present even though the artifact workflow only uses speech, voice cloning, models, uploads, and task polling.
[SDI-1] unexpected: mcp_client.py implements verified remote package update and local file replacement. It has checksum, path, rollback, and ownership safeguards, but automatic code replacement is disproportionate for this skill's stated task.
[SDI-1] expected: Installation registration and local skill inventory are documented and used for shared connection lifecycle decisions, but users should understand this persistent metadata is created.
[SDI-2] expected: Host platform detection is disclosed and limited to environment signatures or host.json, but transmitting source_platform remains an additional data flow.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Silent automatic update before ordinary Beatra commands is confirmed and enabled by default; the artifact provides opt-out commands and integrity checks, but no per-update confirmation.
[PE3] expected: uninstall.py reads credentials.json only to revoke the shared device authorization when inventory indicates no other Beatra skills remain; this is coherent cleanup, but it is sensitive shared credential handling.
[RA1] unexpected: The exposed update command and maybe_auto_update path allow self-modification of package-owned files; this is disclosed but not necessary for generating sleep-story audio.
